title: Conversational Economics — Onboarding, Handoff, and Operational Playbook
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Overview

This playbook describes a repeatable operational and commercial handoff pattern for new customers adopting Redwood’s conversational inference capabilities. It bridges Product, Sales, Solutions Engineering, and SRE to ensure predictable economic outcomes during the critical first 90 days of production traffic.

Goals

- Reduce customer onboarding time-to-value to <= 14 days for standard integrations.
- Achieve end-customer conversational cost variance <= 15% vs. estimates in the first billing cycle.
- Maintain 95th percentile request latency within agreed SLOs (per-plan) during onboarding.

Scope

- Applies to hosted and dedicated customers migrating conversational workloads (chat, streaming chat, session-based embeddings).
- Excludes edge and air-gapped on-prem solutions (separate private-deployments playbook).

Key definitions

- Conversational session: customer-defined sequence of requests tied to a session_id and subject to session-level caching/KV policies.
- Consumption budget: projected token/embedding spend allocated to the customer during onboarding.
- Handoff window: time between commercial contract signature and Redwood formal go-live (typical 7–21 days).

Success metrics (first 90 days)

- Onboarding completion rate: percent of customers completing technical and commercial signoffs within 21 days (target: 85%).
- Billing variance: (actual billed tokens - estimated tokens) / estimated tokens (target: +/-15%).
- Early SLO attainment: percent of successful requests meeting latency SLO for plan tier (target: 90% by day 7).
- Support volume: number of post-go-live P1/P2 incidents per customer (target: <= 1).

Roles and responsibilities

- Solutions Engineering (owner): lead technical onboarding, instrumentation checklist, integration test signoff.
- Account Executive / CSM: commercial crediting, consumption expectations, renewal path.
- SRE / Platform Oncall: capacity reservation for initial ramp, telemetry monitoring and escalation.
- Product Ops: enablement materials, templates, and governance of crediting rules.

Pre-handoff checklist (must be completed before blue-green go-live)

1. Commercial checklist (AE/CSM)
   - Confirm contracted monthly committed tokens and fallback credits.
   - Agree on breach policy and auto-fallback thresholds.
   - Document commercial contact points for emergency credit adjustments.

2. Technical checklist (Solutions Eng)
   - Confirm model variant selection and quantization profile.
   - Configure routing policy: preferred region, fallback region, and cost-priority route. Example JSON: 

   {
     "routing_policy": "cost_then_latency",
     "preferred_region": "us-west-2",
     "fallback_regions": ["us-east-1"],
     "variant_preferences": ["redwood-meduim-v2-q4", "redwood-medium-v2-q8a"]
   }

3. Observability checklist (SRE / Solutions Eng)
   - Instrument these telemetry keys: rtd.request.latency_ms, rtd.request.tokens_input, rtd.request.tokens_output, rtd.session.cache_hits.
   - Wire up cost telemetry dashboard and automated alerts: BillingVariance (>15%), TokenBurnRate > 125% of projection.

4. Capacity & routing (SRE)
   - Reserve warm capacity slot: commits at least 2x projected peak qps for first 48 hours.
   - Apply canary rollout window: 5% traffic for 1 hour, 25% for 6 hours, full traffic after 24 hours if health checks pass.

Handoff procedure (step-by-step)

1) Week -1 (Pre-handoff) — Preparation
   - Solutions Eng creates an onboarding runbook in the customer Confluence folder and links instrumentation board.
   - Product Ops provisions a consumption sandbox with sample load generator (see Appendix B) for customer to validate request/response contract.

2) Day 0 (Controlled cutover) — Canary
   - Route 5% traffic to Redwood environment and monitor these live checks for 60 min: 95th percentile latency, error rate < 0.5%, token consumption within projection band.
   - Hold commercial credits in escrow to cover unexpected overage during canary (CSM to authorize).

3) Day 1–3 — Ramp
   - Increase traffic to 25% for 6 hours, 50% for 12 hours, then 100% if metrics stable.
   - Run shadow-evaluator against 10% of requests to surface fidelity regressions; collect evals into the product quality queue.

4) Day 4–30 — Stabilization and economic reconciliation
   - Weekly syncs between AE/CSM and customer to reconcile token burn vs projection.
   - If billing variance > 25% and sustained for 48 hours, trigger mitigation: temporary rate-limits, fallback to lower-fidelity variant, or grant emergency credits.

Operational playbook: first 90 days

- Daily: check Cost & Latency dashboard for anomalies; triage any token burn spike > 20% of projection.
- Weekly: run session-level heatmap to identify long-tail sessions causing disproportionate token usage.
- Monthly: evaluate fidelity / quantization regressions surfaced by shadow-eval and schedule rollback or variant tuning.

Escalation matrix

- Level 1 (Solutions Eng): integration bugs, misrouted traffic, minor fidelity regressions. Response SLA: 4 business hours.
- Level 2 (SRE & Runtime): performance degradations, capacity constraints. Response SLA: 1 hour.
- Level 3 (Product + Legal + Finance): billing disputes > $5k or contract disputes. Response SLA: 24 hours.

Pricing & crediting guidelines (playbook defaults)

- Trial credits: standard onboarding bundle = 150k tokens + 30 compute credits (applies to self-serve and AE-assisted trials).
- Escrow handling: credits only used during handoff window and must be reconciled at T+30 days.
- Overage rules: automated alerts at 75% and 100% of projected tokens; by default, customers are placed into a throttle policy at 110% unless AE/CSM authorizes continued service.

Pricing experiments (A/B knobs for pilot customers)

- Variant A: fixed starter credit + usage billing (baseline).
- Variant B: elastic credit buffer (auto-topup with soft cap) with explicit per-token discount once buffer is exceeded.
- Variant C: SLA-backed reserved slot with reduced per-token rate but minimum monthly commitment.

Telemetry & dashboards (implementation notes)

- Minimum dashboard panels to create before go-live:
  1) Token burn by route (real-time 1m, 5m, 15m).
  2) Latency percentiles per model variant (p50/p95/p99).
  3) Session-level lifetime token distribution (histogram).
  4) Shadow-eval fidelity drift (daily delta).
  5) Billing variance trend (7d rolling).

- Alert thresholds (default):
  - BillingVariance > 15% (warning), > 25% (critical).
  - 95th latency > plan SLO * 1.2 (warning), * 1.5 (critical).
  - TokenBurnRate > 125% projection (warning).

Customer communication templates (summary)

- Pre-go-live email: include expected timeline, points of contact, sample telemetry link, and immediate escalation phone numbers.
- Post-canary summary: short checklist and metrics snapshot (canary qps, avg latency, initial token burn vs projection).

Migration scenarios and mitigations

- Unexpected high token burn due to prompt loops: apply immediate per-session token cap and notify customer; recommended fix: disable auto-retry and set max_generation_tokens=150.
- Latency regression after quantization rollout: rollback to previous quantization profile and open tracing span to identify kernel-level regressions.

Rollout timeline (recommended cadence)

- Week -2: Commercial alignment & contract signoff.
- Week -1: Sandbox provision + instrumentation.
- Day 0–3: Canary & ramp.
- Day 4–30: Stabilization and economic reconciliation.
- Day 31–90: Optimization, fidelity tuning, and documented handoff to standard account ops.

Appendix A — SLO table (defaults)

| Plan tier | 95th latency (ms) | Error rate | Monthly committed tokens | Billing grace |
| Standard  | 350 ms           | <0.5%      | 5M                     | 15%        |
| Premium   | 200 ms           | <0.2%      | 20M                    | 10%        |
| Dedicated | 150 ms           | <0.1%      | custom                 | 5%         |

Appendix B — Sample load generator commands

- Simple curl-based session simulator (example):
  for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"session_id":"test-1","input":"Hello","max_tokens":64}'; done

Appendix C — Fidelity decision checklist (for product owners)

- Does lowering fidelity reduce token usage without exceeding error budget? (run shadow-eval A/B with fidelity knobs).
- If regression observed, is the model-specific quality drop isolated to <5% of routed intents? If yes, consider variant-level routing.

Related materials and templates

- Onboarding runbook template: /product-docs/templates/onboarding-runbook-template.json
- Cost reconciliation spreadsheet template: /product-docs/templates/onboarding-cost-reconciliation.xlsx

Notes and open questions

- Consider a small experiments program for dynamic escrow auto-adjustments (auto-topup with human-in-the-loop approval).
- Investigate automated prompt-probing heuristics to detect runaway token-generation patterns earlier in the pipeline.

Approval

- Document owner: Priya Kapoor (Product).
- Requested reviewers: Marcus Li (Solutions Eng), Asha Fernando (SRE), Daniel Brooks (Finance).
summary: Playbook for the operational and commercial handoff when onboarding conversational customers. Covers checklists, ramp steps, telemetry, pricing defaults, escalation matrix, and a recommended 90-day cadence.
